key_insight: Euclid-MCP adds a standardized MCP interface for delegating deterministic Horn-clause reasoning to SWI-Prolog, giving LLMs a reliable way to reason with proof traces instead of hallucinating.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical neuro-symbolic substrate for compliance, security, and other rule-based workflows where exact inference, auditability, and reproducibility matter.
method: Defines Euclid-IR, a human-readable intermediate representation for Horn-clause logic that LLMs can generate and backends can compile.
Exposes a compact translate-run-inspect-repair tool loop through an MCP server connected to SWI-Prolog.
Supports proof traces and derivation logs so clients can inspect and correct logical executions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on a realistic IT security and compliance task, where LLMs worked on small knowledge bases but hallucinated on larger ones, while Euclid-MCP returned exact answers with lower latency and more compact outputs.
watch_item: Performance and correctness depend on the quality of the Euclid-IR translation and the completeness of the underlying rule base, so malformed or incomplete specifications can still limit results.
paper_title: Euclid-MCP: A Model Context Protocol Server for Deterministic Logical Reasoning via Prolog
